snippet.title: Taste 90 Years of LA Deli History | Canter’s – Los Angeles
snippet.description:
Meet your host: Marc. Third-generation owner of Canter's Deli, he’s spent his life inside one of LA’s most iconic institutions, carrying forward a story that started long before him.

If you want to understand Los Angeles, don’t just chase what’s new. Sit at the counter. Order something that’s been on the menu for decades. Listen to the stories that only exist because someone stayed.

Canter’s isn’t just a deli. It’s late nights, neon lights, and booths that have seen everything. Musicians, actors, locals, regulars. The kind of place where history doesn’t sit on a wall, it lives in the room.

This isn’t just a meal. It’s a walk through 90 years of LA, told by someone who’s part of it. Pastrami, matzo ball soup, black and white cookies, and the stories behind it all.

Book a tasting with Marc and you’ll see the city differently. Not just where to go, but what’s lasted. The places that don’t change, even when everything around them does.

snippet.title: Tuma's Venice Skate Experience
snippet.description:
Meet your host: Tuma. A third-generation Z-Boy who grew up skating these parks, these cracks, these same stretches of Venice pavement where everybody starts unsure.

If you want to understand Venice, don’t start with the beach. Start with the pavement. Tuma knows Venice. By feel. By timing. By showing up. Nobody shows up good. Everyone learns the hard way. Falling is part of it. So is getting back up.

Skating here isn’t about tricks for the camera. It’s about timing. About knowing when to go, when to wait, and when to just roll around and feel the ground under your feet. It’s about respect. For the space. For the people who’ve been showing up long before you. And for yourself while you’re figuring it out.

Book a session with Tuma and you’ll see the park differently. Where beginners usually start. Where to stand so you’re not in the way. And where Dogtown begins and ends.

This is Venice culture in real time. Open. Shared. Passed hand to hand. Just roll when you’re ready.

And afterward, if you want to grab a coffee or want to know where to get something to eat, he’ll point you in the right direction.

Just don’t ask him if its called “Dogtown” because of all the cute pups.

snippet.title: Bring it Home Documentary | Teaser Trailer
snippet.description:
How the Airbnb travel grant recipients find their place.

Bring It Home is a short documentary following six Olympic and Paralympic hopefuls as they train, travel, and compete around the world on the road to Milano Cortina 2026. 

Through the Airbnb Athlete Travel Grant, athletes receive support to help cover stays while training and competing internationally. From limited access to snow to financial challenges, each story reveals what it takes to stay focused, grounded, and in the race for a place at the Olympic & Paralympic Winter Games.

Featured grant recipients:
Donovan Carrillo – Figure Skating (Mexico)
Laura Vargas – Skeleton (Colombia)
Edson Bindilatti – Bobsled (Brazil)
Andrea Macri – Para Ice Hockey (Italy)
Joanna Butterfield – Wheelchair Curling (GB)
Asa Toyoda – Snowboarding (Japan)

Film Credits
Bring It Home was directed by Walter Thompson-Hernández
Cinematography by Mitchell Mahar Perrin
Edited by Nick Deliberto

About the Airbnb Athlete Travel Grant
The Airbnb Athlete Travel Grant helps Olympic & Paralympic hopefuls access places to stay while training and competing worldwide.

Learn more about Airbnb’s partnership with the Olympic & Paralympic Games: https://www.olympics.com/ioc/partners/airbnb

snippet.title: Dear LA
snippet.description:
One year after the Palisades and Eaton fires, local Airbnb hosts and guests reflect on why they love Los Angeles and discuss how communities stepped up before, during, and after the 2025 wildfires.

With the help from partners and donors, Airbnb.org funded  free, emergency housing for nearly 24,000 people displaced by the fires—for over 77,000 total nights.

Airbnb.org committed $16 million to Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles to help with long-term recovery and rebuilding.

Learn more: http://www.airbnb.org/dearla

snippet.title: Gift a Night
snippet.description:
Nights are special. They’re a time for dinner, dog walks, and bedtime stories. But for the millions displaced by disasters each year, nightly joys are often left behind.

This year, Airbnb.org responded to more than 50 disasters around the world and more than 33,000 people received free, emergency housing totaling more than 95,000 nights. 

For $110, you can give one night of emergency housing to a family during a crisis. Airbnb will match your one-time donation through December 31, doubling your impact.

Help us bring a little more home to people when they need it most at the link below:

http://www.airbnb.org/giftanight

snippet.title: Airbnb | 宿泊先いろいろ 日本いろいろ | Weekend
snippet.description:
長野県白馬村のゲレンデを一望できる貸別荘に、写真家の大野隼男が友人グループと滞在。仲間が旅を楽しむ様子を写真に収めました。スキー場まで徒歩10分と、スノーレジャーにぴったりのこの宿泊先。さらに眺めも抜群で、広々としたリビングやお風呂の窓からは息をのむような一面の銀世界が広がります。お部屋でも、屋外でも、冬を満喫できる宿泊先です。Airbnbなら何万ものなかから次の旅にぴったりの宿泊先が見つかります。この冬は、まだ知らない、わくわくするような日本を体験しにいきませんか？

Airbnb（エアビーアンドビー）について
Airbnbのコミュニティは、2人のホストがサンフランシスコの自宅に3人のゲストを迎えた2008年に生まれ、以来、何百万ものホストに支えられ、世界中のほぼすべての国と地域で8億人を超えるゲストをお迎えしてきました。Airbnbのホストは、今日もまたオリジナリティあふれる滞在とユニークな体験を提供しており、ゲストが心のつながりと居心地の良さとともに世界を体験することを可能にしています。

キャンペーンについて　
さまざまな写真家とその家族や友達をAirbnbの旅に招待。その旅を彼ら彼女らのスタイルで、自由に写真に収めてもらいました。日本ならではの古民家からモダンな現代建築の家まで、その宿泊先ならではの風景や思い出が写真の一枚一枚から感じられます。ユニークな音楽とともにその写真を編集し映像化することで、Airbnbでしか味わえない豊かで楽しい旅行を表現しています。宿泊先いろいろ、日本いろいろ。宿泊先の数だけ、新しい日本の旅があなたを待っているのです。

snippet.title: The Benn family sticks together after the wildfires
snippet.description:
Known as the music family of Altadena, the Benns have lived in the area since the 1950s and regularly perform at community events around town. The Eaton fire took two homes they’d owned for generations.

Eleven family members were able to stay together in an Airbnb for free while they figured out next steps. “Getting into a house altogether was crucial for this time, especially because we've got folks with mobility issues and little ones,” said Loren, the eldest of the Benns’ seven children. At the Airbnb, they had their first home-cooked meal since the wildfires, and the youngest grandchild took his first steps. The Benns plan to return to Altadena and reconnect with their community.

Airbnb.org has provided emergency housing for more than 22,000 people displaced by the LA wildfires. Learn more at airbnb.org/helpla

snippet.description:
Eshele is a therapist who grew up in Altadena, CA, where she’s also raised her 11-year-old son, Brayden. She, her mother, and her two sisters all lost their homes in the wildfires. While staying in emergency housing for free through Airbnb.org, Eshele continued working to provide mental health services to her community, and Brayden was able to continue his dance classes.

“Being in this space has allowed me to breathe, and rest, and know that I’m protected and taken care of,” Eshele said.

snippet.title: Paralympian keeps Paris 2024 dreams alive after Brazil floods
snippet.description:
Earlier this year, massive floods displaced 600,000 people and destroyed 200,000 homes in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. 

Two-time Paralympic fencer Vanderson Chaves was among those forced to evacuate. He lost everything in his home, including his fencing equipment, medals, and passport, and thought he might miss his chance to qualify for the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games.

Airbnb.org provided Vanderson free, temporary housing in a wheelchair-accessible home near his training center, which allowed him to keep preparing for the Games. 

During his Airbnb.org stay, Vanderson learned that he made Brazil’s Paralympic team. The Paralympics start today and you can watch Vanderson compete starting September 3 at 13:00 CET.

Learn more about how http://www.airbnb.org has supported hundreds of thousands of people like Vanderson with free, temporary housing.

After Ula and her family left Syria to start a new life in Turkey, an earthquake destroyed their home in 2023. Find out how hosts like Farouk were able to help them and others in a similar situation by opening their homes through Airbnb.org.

This video was produced for us by BBC StoryWorks. 

Airbnb.org is a nonprofit organization that provides free, temporary housing for people displaced by disaster and conflict around the world. Your donation can help provide even more people with housing after a crisis. 

Donate at http://www.airbnb.org

snippet.title: Supporting earthquake survivors from Türkiye and Syria | Airbnb.org
snippet.description:
“I have been working with humanitarian organizations for almost eight years. The earthquake was the first time that I was the one who needed assistance from others.”

Elif and fellow humanitarian aid workers for global nonprofit GOAL were among those who lost their homes in the earthquakes that hit Türkiye and Syria in February 2023. Airbnb.org helped connect them to emergency  housing so they could continue their life-saving work. 

Airbnb.org is a nonprofit organization that provides free temporary housing for people in large-scale crises around the world. Your donation makes a difference. Donate at airbnb.org.

snippet.title: What a Difference a Day Makes | Countryside
snippet.description:
Craving a much-needed snow day, Joyce and her friends traded in the sunny skies of LA for the big skies of Montana. They headed north to Bob's cabin, just outside Bozeman. It was the perfect rustic weekend, filled with hikes through the Bridger Mountains, epic snowballs fights, and time spent by the fire. This is just one of millions of trips made possible by Airbnb Categories.

PHOTOGRAPHER
Joyce Kim

HOME

Airbnb was born in 2008 when two Hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to millions of Hosts who have welcomed over 800 million guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN
We invited photographers to take trips on Airbnb with their family and friends, shoot photos of their stays, and send them back to us. They chose homes from across a range of our new categories, from castles, to homes with amazing pools, to the Arctic. We edited the photos together with familiar songs and the result captures the unique experience of traveling on Airbnb, made possible by these new categories.

snippet.title: Forging friendship in the aftermath of the Camp Fire | Airbnb.org
snippet.description:
“A home, to me, is where your family is.” 

After the Camp Fire devastated the town of Paradise in northern California, people in nearby communities signed up to provide temporary housing through Airbnb’s Open Homes program. Melissa and her family found shelter with Cinde, an Airbnb Host and Sacramento entrepreneur. 

In December 2020, the Airbnb Open Homes program transitioned to Airbnb.org. Airbnb.org is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to facilitating emergency stays for people in large-scale crises around the world. Your donation makes a difference. Donate at airbnb.org.

snippet.title: Supporting relief workers providing long-term aid in Indonesia | Airbnb.org
snippet.description:
“We work for the community, we work from the heart.” 

In August 2018, a string of earthquakes and hundreds of aftershocks rattled the Indonesian island of Lombok. Hundreds of lives were lost and 80% of structures were damaged. The Mercy Corps Indonesia response team was deployed to the remote island to help rebuild. While fulfilling their vital mission, the team was hosted in an Airbnb villa, which they used as a base camp for over a year.

Airbnb.org is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that facilitates emergency stays for people in large-scale crises around the world. Your donation makes a difference. Donate at airbnb.org.

snippet.title: Tranquilo | Piscinas Incríveis
snippet.description:
Paz e suas amigas queriam um fim de semana absolutamente tranquilo. A casa em meio à floresta em Teresópolis, no Rio de Janeiro, foi o lugar perfeito para desconectar da vida de mãe, profissional e estudante. Tudo começou com uma recepção calorosa, com um bolo feito e presenteado pela anfitriã. Depois, a vida girou em torno da piscina. Foi ali que elas nadaram, relaxaram, tomaram sol e comeram. Entre animais silvestres e uma paisagem inspiradora, as amigas viveram momentos livres de preocupação, rindo, falando besteira ou tendo conversas profundas em volta da fogueira. Foram só dois dias. Mas foi o suficiente para renovar as energias e as amizades. A única preocupação agora é saber quando elas vão poder voltar.

MÚSICA
Tranquilo – Thalma de Freitas

FOTÓGRAFA
Paz Olivares Droguett

ACOMODAÇÃO
https://www.airbnb.com.br/rooms/31829321
 
SOBRE O AIRBNB
O Airbnb nasceu em 2007, quando dois anfitriões receberam três hóspedes em sua casa em São Francisco. Hoje, a plataforma conta com 4 milhões de anfitriões que já receberam mais de 1,5 bilhão de hóspedes em quase todos os países do mundo. Todos os dias, os anfitriões oferecem acomodações e experiências únicas que possibilitam que os viajantes conheçam outras comunidades de uma forma mais autêntica.

SOBRE A CAMPANHA
Convidamos fotógrafos para se hospedarem com suas famílias e amigos através do Airbnb, registrarem suas experiências e compartilharem as imagens conosco. Eles escolheram as acomodações dentre as várias opções oferecidas pelas nossas categorias, de castelos a casas com piscinas incríveis até chalés no Ártico. Em seguida, editamos as fotos com músicas conhecidas e o resultado revela a experiência única que é viajar com o Airbnb, tendo nossas categorias como ponto de partida.

snippet.title: An Ode To Black Travel | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Black travel has been an integral part of Black history, throughout the ages. And Airbnb’s Black employee resource group, known as Black@, are here to honor this never-ending journey, in the form of a video essay.

Whether it’s the pursuit of prosperity, the forward movement of civil Rights marchers, or just everyday adventurers packing their bags and chasing new discoveries, the trailblazing spirit has always been alive and well in our community, all across the diaspora. None of which would be possible without Black people hosting one another, as we all need safe spaces where we’re free to be our best selves.

That’s when joy happens, inspiration happens, culture happens—and when all of that happens, so does history.

The best part is, this is just the beginning. Come find us on Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/blackatairbnb/.

snippet.title: Be transported to Kenya with refugee athletes at the Tegla Loroupe Training Centre I Airbnb
snippet.description:
Take a deep dive into our daily life of refugee athletes training for the Olympic Games Tokyo 2020, in the heart of Kenya. For this airbnb Online Experience, catch a glimpse into where we get in shape, and equip ourselves with tools for life, at the Tegla Loroupe Training Centre. A few of us share our personal and inspiring life stories; go through a 20-minute workout, and interact with the guests on the experience, with a questions and answers section at the end.

All the proceeds of this event are donated directly to the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation.

The airbnb virtual experience was hosted live from the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation and Training Centre (based in Ngong Nairobi). The Foundation promotes peace-building, livelihood and the resilience of people affected by violence and vulnerable to conflicts and civil strife in the world. 19 athletes come from Kakuma Refugee Camps, and are currently training at the center aiming to be part of the Refugee Olympic Team Tokyo 2020.

https://teglapeace.org/

snippet.title: Designed to Host
snippet.description:
FROM YOUR HOST: Shea McGee, founder and chief creative officer of Studio McGee

Whether I’m hosting an al fresco dinner with friends or welcoming extended family for a long weekend, one of the most gratifying elements of designing my dream home has been sharing it with others. Good design invites you in and greets you like a familiar hug, making a space and the moments experienced there meaningful and memorable – just as a good host does.  
 
As we look forward to gathering and traveling again, there’s no time like the present to get your home guest-ready. 
 
Join me for a discussion about the art of hospitality, where I’ll walk you through my process for creating spaces where everyone feels at home, no matter how far they’ve traveled. Whether you’re an Airbnb Host looking to create a five-star space for guests, or simply hoping to freshen up your approach to hosting friends, you’re sure to walk away with a refreshed perspective on how to use everyday elements to set the stage for memorable spaces. 
 
Let’s make life – and its hosted moments – beautiful.

This is a social impact experience where 100% of what you pay for this experience goes to the IIDA Foundation.

FIND OUT MORE
abnb.co/howtohost

ABOUT THE IIDA FOUNDATION
The IIDA Foundation is a philanthropic organization with a mission to drive innovation and advancements in the commercial interior design field. The Foundation seeks to make a meaningful impact through supporting grants and funding opportunities, and continued support of education, research, outreach, and the fostering of an innovative and inclusive design community.

SUBSCRIBE
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCCww... 

ABOUT AIRBNB
Airbnb is a community based on connection and belonging—a community that was born in 2008 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to 4 million hosts who have welcomed over 800 million guest arrivals to about 100,000 cities in almost every country and region across the globe. Hosts on Airbnb are everyday people who share their worlds to provide guests with the feeling of connection and being at home. At Airbnb, we believe that hosts, guests and the communities where we operate are all stakeholders we have a responsibility to serve, and that by serving them alongside our employees and investors, we will build an enduringly successful company.

snippet.title: A Very Kardashian Christmas
snippet.description:
FROM YOUR HOSTS: KRIS JENNER AND JEFFREY LEATHAM

More is more, I always say – especially when it comes to holiday home décor. The bigger, the brighter, the bolder, the better. But you can do a lot with a little, too.

Join me and Jeff Leatham – friend, collaborator and artistic decorator who’s helped me bring my holiday dreams to life over the years – for a décor discussion to remember. We’ll talk about where we get our inspiration for our beautiful arrangements, the benefit of a well-defined design theme and the joy of creating a holiday space that sparkles.

Let’s. get. festive.
 
This is a social impact experience where 100% of paid guest bookings for this experience goes to The Watts Empowerment Center.

About the organization: Watts Empowerment Center
The Watts Empowerment Center is the no. 1 most active community center in Los Angeles. This 12,900 square foot state-of-the-art facility is committed to the children, youth, and families within Watts Housing Projects and offers resources from sports leagues and performing arts studios to after-school tutoring and resume-building workshops and more.
 
Photo credit: Carlos Eric Lopez Studios
carlosericlopez.com | @carlosericlopez

snippet.title: Introducing Airbnb.org
snippet.description:
A new nonprofit that opens homes in times of crisis. Airbnb.org is inspired by our host community, and we’re proud to say it began eight years ago with the actions of a single host—Shell.

After Hurricane Sandy struck in 2012, Shell sprang into action, sharing her home with a family forced to evacuate theirs. Her generosity inspired thousands of other hosts to do the same, and since then, over 75,000 people in 104 countries have been housed during emergencies.

We are now formalizing these efforts with the creation of Airbnb.org, an independent, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that works in partnership with global NGOs and relief organizations to provide emergency stays for people when they need it most.

snippet.title: Bringing Activism to the Dinner Table with Jaden Smith
snippet.description:
FROM YOUR HOSTS: Artist and Activist Jaden Smith and Dr. Phillip Atiba Goff, co-founder and CEO of the Center for Policy Equity, and a Professor of African-American Studies and Psychology at Yale University

Though bringing family together may look different this year, one tradition is sure to remain - spirited debates. Given the imminent election and current climate, keeping the peace at holiday dinner isn’t always guaranteed.

That’s why I’m excited to sit with my friend, Dr. Phillip Atiba Goff, to chat about how we can navigate these difficult conversations. I’m no stranger to frank and insightful family dialogue. I want to share some of the things I’ve learned about navigating uncomfortable conversations with you. We’ll chat about how we can have peaceful and productive debates with loved ones whose views may differ from our own. And, of course, answer any questions you may have ahead of the holiday season.

Together, we hope to create room to bring activism to the dinner table and facilitate healthy debate among family.

This is a social impact experience where 100% of what you pay for this experience goes to Vote.org.

snippet.title: How to be a Social Problem Solver
snippet.description:
We live in a big, beautiful world, full of possibility. And full of problems just waiting to be solved.

If there’s anything our family has learned during our combined years of activism and advocacy, it’s that it’s never too soon (and never too late!) to be the change you want to see in the world. But sometimes it’s hard to know where to start, especially when you’re young.

Join us for a discussion with social problem solver Marley, where we’ll talk about her passion for equity, inclusivity and social change. Bring a problem in need of solving or a cause that’s close to your heart, and we’ll walk you through the best first (or next!) step to take. We can’t wait to watch you change the world.

snippet.title: Decoding the Science of 2020 with Bill Nye
snippet.description:
Science is the process and the body of knowledge that enables us humans to know nature. So far, it’s the best idea humans have ever had.

Let’s spend some time together uncovering the science that affects our everyday lives. We’ll explore three topics particularly relevant to the here and now: the science of skin color, the impact of climate change and the transmission of coronavirus. We’ll examine molecules and maps, evaluate atmospheres and aerospace, and experiment with particles and powders, all in the name of science.

snippet.title: My ‘Texican’ Kitchen with Eva Longoria
snippet.description:
I have always been passionate about food, love to cook for my family and friends, and have perfected timeless classics that celebrate my heritage.

As a proud Mexican-American Texan — or ‘Texican’, as I like to say — I was raised on some of the most delicious and inspired meals, and I find that there’s no better place to gather with those you love than in the kitchen or around the table.

During my cooking class, I’ll teach you one of my most cherished recipes and together we’ll celebrate the beauty and the legacy of Hispanic culture.

snippet.title: A Very Kardashian Christmas
snippet.description:
FROM YOUR HOSTS: KRIS JENNER AND JEFFREY LEATHAM

More is more, I always say – especially when it comes to holiday home décor. The bigger, the brighter, the bolder, the better. But you can do a lot with a little, too.

Join me and Jeff Leatham – friend, collaborator and artistic decorator who’s helped me bring my holiday dreams to life over the years – for a décor discussion to remember. We’ll talk about where we get our inspiration for our beautiful arrangements, the benefit of a well-defined design theme and the joy of creating a holiday space that sparkles.

Let’s. get. festive.
 
This is a social impact experience where 100% of paid guest bookings for this experience goes to The Watts Empowerment Center.

Skateboarding legend Tony Hawk welcomes you to his personal vert ramp for live demos and discussion about the evolution of the sport. Join him and his friends—including Bucky Lasek, Andy Macdonald, and Sky Brown—to learn the moves that propelled skateboarding to its Olympic debut.

This online experience is part of the summer 2020 festival of Olympian and Paralympian online experiences, hosted by Airbnb in partnership with the Olympics and Paralympics. snippet.title: Back From the Antarctic Sabbatical | Only On | Airbnb
snippet.description:
In December of 2019, five passionate volunteers – selected from more than 140,000 applicants – got to experience the vast beauty of the Great White Continent first hand, as part of the Antarctic Sabbatical.  

Their mission? To assist British environmental scientist Kirstie Jones-Williams with her ground-breaking research into microplastics – and their potential pollution of Earth’s last great wilderness. During their visit, the Airbnb volunteers collected multiple snow samples from remote sites, as well as helping Jones-Williams process and analyse them in her Antarctic lab.

snippet.title: Tiny Treasures | Check-In to the Trend | Airbnb
snippet.description:
On this episode of Check-In to the Trend, The Tiny Chef (https://www.instagram.com/thetinychefshow/) brings his culinary passion and affinity for kitchen design to Airbnb. For the first time ever, four travelers and fellow miniature food enthusiasts are able to get an insider’s look at The Chef’s tree stump home -- including his beautiful kitchen and “sheeshell sink”. To celebrate our newest and tiniest host, I met up with Chef to discuss how food travel is booming with Airbnb guests and take a look at some other teeny kitchens that will excite you enough to cook your biggest cravings.

The Airbnbs and Experiences in this episode are:
Meet & Eat with The Tiny Chef (Glendale, CA)

snippet.title: Beyond Big Cities: Kamaishi, Japan | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Devastated by the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami in 2011, the city of Kamaishi has come together to rebuild over the past eight years. In 2019 Kamaishi was awarded the honor of being a host city for the largest rugby tournament in the world. With a new spotlight on their city, the people of Kamaishi are turning to tourism as a way to further revitalize the city, share their culture and traditions, and make connections with guests from across the world. 

One major way they’re able to do that is by tapping into Airbnb’s global network of travelers. Over the course of the tournament, Airbnb guest arrivals around Kamaishi increased by 180%*.

*Internal Stays guest arrival data for Iwate Prefecture, Sept. 2019 - Nov. 2019 vs. Sept. 2018 - Nov. 2018

snippet.title: Spooky Encounters | Check-In to the Trend | Airbnb
snippet.description:
As travelers get into the Halloween spirit, many are also bringing their thrills to life through haunted stays and Airbnb Experiences. In fact, more than 9,000 guests have stayed in haunted homes*, and spooky Experience bookings went up 174 percent since last year**. And interestingly enough, female travelers are the ones booking them the most***.

In this episode of Check-In to the Trend, Airbnb Trend Expert, Ali Killam, pays a visit to a civil-war era house outside Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, to see why paranormal encounters are such a draw to travelers.

The Airbnbs and Experiences in this episode are:
Gettysburg Historic Lookout House-1920's Darb Room (Aspers, PA)
Paranormal Tour of the U.S. Southwest (Las Vegas, NV)
Explore the Snake Cave & Bacalar (Tulum, Mexico)
Amsterdam Movie Prosthetics (Amsterdam, Netherlands)
Speakeasy Murder Mystery (Chicago, IL)
Mentalist's Mysteries (Florence, Italy) 

*Based on Airbnb internal data of guest arrivals to homes including keywords (haunted, spooky, paranormal, etc.) from September 2018 to September 2019.

**Based on Airbnb internal data of year-over-year growth of bookings of Experiences including keywords (haunted, spooky, paranormal, etc.) from September 2018 to September 2019.

***Based on Airbnb internal data of guest arrivals to and bookings of homes and Experiences including keywords (haunted, spooky, paranormal, etc.) based on gender from September 2018 to September 2019.

snippet.title: Goodyear Blimp | Only On | Airbnb
snippet.description:
To celebrate the spirit of the college football pastime and its fans, Goodyear is listing the famous Blimp on Airbnb, with three one-night stays that will be available for booking leading up to the college football rivalry game in Ann Arbor, MI, on October 26. 

Beginning October 15, passionate fans will be able to request to book the Blimp for a one-night stay in Mogadore, Ohio, on October 22, 23, or 24. 

Learn more: Airbnb.com/blimp

snippet.title: Regal Retreats | Check-In to the Trend | Airbnb
snippet.description:
For the first time ever, Highclere Castle - the home of Downton Abbey - has opened its doors to guests to spend the night, but travelers have been seeking ways to bring their fairytales to life by staying in castles on Airbnb. In fact, in the last year alone, guests have searched for castles more than 21 million times on Airbnb*.

In this episode of Check-In to the Trend, Airbnb Trend Expert, Ali Killam pays a visit to Warwickshire, UK to see why regal retreats are trending with travelers.

The Airbnbs included in this episode are:

The East Gate and St Peter's Chapel (Warwickshire, UK)
Old Presbytery - 17th Century (Langoiran, France)
Royal Heritage Residency (Jaisalmer, India)
Holiday Cottage inside a Castle (Castellterçol, Spain)
Cozy Storybook Castle (Ellington, CT)
Bishops Palace Ballarat (Lake Wendouree, Australia)

*Based on Airbnb internal data of guest searches using the castle listing type from September 2018 to September 2019.

FIND OUT MORE
https://www.airbnb.com/regalretreats

READ MORE:

snippet.title: Upcycled Getaways | Check-In to the Trend | Airbnb
snippet.description:
In this episode of Check-In to the Trend, Airbnb Trend Expert, Ali Killam, heads to the UK to see why hosts are increasingly sharing homes made from reclaimed – or upcycled – materials. In fact, spaces built with upcycled materials have increased by 175 percent on Airbnb over the last four years*.

The Airbnb homes included in this episode are:

Magic Cottage - Cosy Wood Cabin (Fareham, UK)
The Recyclable House Beaufort - Eco Country Getaway (Beaufort, Australia)
Cabana Floripa (Florianópolis, Brazil)
Unique Cob Cottage (Mayne Island, Canada)
Recycled Apartment Close to the Beach (Odeceixe, Portugal)
Tiny Eco Friendly Modern Shipping Containers (Atlanta, GA)

*Based on Airbnb internal data of year-over-year growth of listings including specific keywords (recycled materials, upcycled materials, reclaimed materials, etc.) from August 2015 to August 2019.

snippet.title: Planes, Trains and Airbnbs | Check-In to the Trend | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Waking up in an Apollo 11 replica or a rustic, yet industrially renovated WWII train car seems otherwordly enough to be the subject of our wildest dreams. However, hosts around the world have either recreated or renovated more than 280,000 unique spaces and are sharing them with guests*. From planes and trains to spaceships, these transformed idyllic dwellings have been wishlisted more than 2 million times by travelers on Airbnb**.

In this episode of Check-In to the Trend, Airbnb Trend Expert, Ali Killam pays a visit to Maryville, TN to see why moveable getaways are trending with travelers.

The Airbnbs included in this episode are:

The Original Spice Bus from 1997 Movie Spice World (Isle of Wight, UK)
The Unicorn Room (Coron, Philippines)
Platform1346-WWII Train Car Turned Vacation Spot! (Maryville, TN)
Sleep in a True Plane!  (Saint-Michel-Chef-Chef, France) 
Apollo 11 Spaceship with View of Mt. Cook (Pukaki, New Zealand)


*Based on Airbnb internal data from May 2019 of specific listing types on the platform, that include but are not limited to moveable listing types (38 different types are encapsulated in this number, incl: cabin, shepherd’s hut, bus, castle).
**Based on Airbnb internal data showing growth of new wishlisted listings by listing type (June 1, 2018-May 31, 2019).

snippet.title: Heritage Travel is on the Rise | Check-In to the Trend | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Since 2014, the number of travelers using Airbnb for tracing their roots increased by 500 percent*. And with 74 percent of surveyed U.S. residents interested in taking a genetic test**, along with the rise of at-home genetic tests like 23andMe, it has never been easier to learn about your ancestry.

In this episode of Check-In to the Trend, Airbnb Trend Expert, Ali Killam (@alikillam), takes her dad on their own heritage trip through the English countryside after taking a 23andMe test to explore where they come from with help from Airbnb hosts. 

Homes and Experiences featured in this episode include - 

The Barn Pye Corner Farm (Chesire, England)
Be a farmer for the morning (Rossendale, England)
A Taste of Chester Food Walking Tour (England)

*Airbnb guest reviews with DNA and heritage-related keywords, 2014 vs. 2018
**23andMe commissioned U.S. survey of 1,500 adults, April 2019

snippet.title: Location Reviews April 2019 | Host Q&A | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Airbnb hosts asked the question: “Does Airbnb have any plans to rephrase the location category in reviews? Location reviews seem to depend on a guest’s opinion, rather than a standard of service.” Yes! In fact, we recently published a blog post recapping the improvements we’ve made to the review system. Now, when a guest rates you in the location category, if they give you three stars or fewer, they’ll see an additional question: “Was the listing’s location not described accurately?” So far, this change has led to an increase in the average rating for location. Laura Chambers, Airbnb’s general manager of Homes Host, says it’s also important to clarify that the location category rating doesn’t impact a host’s overall rating or eligibility for Superhost status. She talks more about the fix and other changes that have made reviews more fair for hosts.

snippet.title: Where Fees Go April 2019 | Host Q&A | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Airbnb hosts asked the question: “What does Airbnb do with the hosting fees it collects?” Hosts and guests are usually charged a service fee whenever a booking or Experience is confirmed. The money that’s collected is invested into three big categories—community support, marketing, and product development—to help support hosts. In the past year, for instance, Airbnb built a new process online so that hosts can get assistance in whichever way they prefer—our online chat system or on the phone—more quickly. Next is marketing, which helps Airbnb stay top of mind for travelers when they’re looking for places to stay and things to do—and, ultimately, help bring you more guests. We focus mainly on three types of marketing: traditional advertising, online, and other campaigns via Airbnb’s website and mobile app. And finally, we’re investing in product development, and building the tools and infrastructure to power hosts’ businesses and to help them succeed.

snippet.title: Host Commitment April 2019 | Host Q&A | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Airbnb hosts asked the question: “What are Airbnb’s top priorities this year and what can hosts expect?” Airbnb makes a clear, simple commitment to hosts: to empower hosts to be successful by providing information, education, and the tools they need; to support hosts by minimizing the instances of things going wrong and, in the rare case that they do, having hosts’ backs; and to build community by helping hosts connect to each other and Airbnb. “Our founder, CEO, and head of Community Brian Chesky wants to make sure our core hosts are taken care of and our employees are incredibly focused on our core host community, especially as we begin to welcome other types of properties such as boutique hotels,” said Laura Chambers, Airbnb’s general manager of Homes Host.

snippet.title: Guest Profile Photos April 2019 | Host Q&A | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Airbnb hosts asked the question: “Will there be any changes with guest profile photos in the future?” In an effort to reduce discrimination, Airbnb recently stopped allowing hosts to see guest profile photos before booking. In this video, hosts in London begin an important dialogue on the issue, with topics ranging from trust and safety to unconscious bias. The discussions illustrate the difficult tension between ensuring hosts feel safe and ensuring Airbnb is a place where everyone belongs. Laura Chambers, Airbnb’s general manager of Homes Host, encouraged hosts to talk candidly about their views, as well as listen to and consider each other’s personal experiences.

snippet.title: Connecting Home & Experience Hosting April 2019 | Host Q&A | Airbnb
snippet.description:
Airbnb hosts asked the question: “How can Homes and Experience hosts link up to offer guests package deals?” “Package deals” won’t be immediately available, but there are a few things we are doing to bring Homes and Experiences hosting closer together. First, both Experiences and home listings show up on a host’s user profile page so the Airbnb community knows if a host offers both. Hosts can also write to guests once they book to promote an Experience. To see what’s on offer, Homes and Experience hosts can connect through local hosting groups and here in Airbnb’s Community Center.

snippet.title: Women Adventuring On Their Own | Check-In to the Trend | Airbnb
snippet.description:
All over the world, we're finding women are making the most of their independent adventures by navigating cities with the help from locals through Airbnb Experiences--more so than men.

Airbnb Trend Expert, Ali Killam (@alikillam), and Jessica Nabongo (@catchmeifyoucan), the first black woman set to travel to every country in the world by October 2019, discuss why they think Airbnb Experiences are so popular amongst solo women.

According to Airbnb booking data (2018 vs. 2017), solo women are booking 10x more History Experiences, 4x more Sports & Wellness Experiences, and 3x more Art Experiences. Ali and Jessica highlight a few Experiences in these categories in New York, including -

Learn how to box with a World Champion

snippet.title: Wheelwrighting | Preserving UK Heritage Crafts | Airbnb
snippet.description:
As a Master Wheelwright, Greg builds and repairs wooden wheels. The craft has been in Greg's family since 1331, going back 17 generations. Today, he makes the carriages for the British royal family, and is now opening up his workshop to visitors to share his craft and allow guests to play a part in making something historical.
